As we wrap up, I want you to take a moment to recognize what you've just experienced. You've walked with me through stories that are raw, honest, and sometimes incredibly tough to hear. What stands out is this: rape culture isn't just about isolated incidents—it's a system that shapes how we see ourselves, each other, and the world around us.
But the stories in Not That Bad aren't here to leave you feeling stuck or hopeless. They're a call to action. A reminder that real change is possible—and that each of us has a role to play.
So, here are a few things I hope you'll carry forward:
Every story of harm deserves to be heard and truly respected. Healing isn't a straight line—it's personal, and it takes time. Justice and accountability look different for everyone, and that's okay. If you're a bystander or an ally, remember—even small actions can make a big difference. Rethinking what it means to be masculine is key to building a kinder, safer world. And real, lasting change? It's messy, it's slow, but it starts with ongoing commitment from all of us.
The truth is, you don't need all the answers to make an impact. Start by listening—really listening—to the people in your life. Believe survivors when they share their stories. Speak up against language and attitudes that downplay harm, even when it's uncomfortable. Support organizations and policies that prioritize prevention, healing, and justice. And remember—your actions, no matter how small, can reach further than you might ever realize.
Challenging rape culture isn't easy—and it certainly isn't quick. But it's necessary. And it's possible. You're not alone in this. Every conversation, every act of empathy, every time you refuse to accept “not that bad” as good enough—you help move us closer to a world where everyone is safe, respected, and free.
Keep going. The future really is shaped by what we do today.
